transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi. It's, um, really nice to meet you. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope it's okay that I came in for this, I know you probably see people with much bigger problems, but... I guess I've just been having a little bit of trouble keeping things organized lately? 

I try really hard to keep on top of it, I promise, but I feel like I just cannot get my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. It's just... my craft supplies, and my due dates, and the receipts, and then my assignment notes... no matter what I do, they all just kind of end up in these piles everywhere. And then I look at them and I just don't know what to do first. 

It's probably just me needing to try a different planner or something, but... does that make sense? Like, is that an okay reason to be here?
When you were a child, did teachers or parents say you were often forgetful, disorganized, or had trouble paying attention?

Um... well, I don't know if I was super disorganized back then, mostly because my mom handled all my folders and stuff for me. But... I mean, I guess I was definitely a little, um, energetic? I hope that's okay to say. 

My mom actually still has some of my old elementary school notes from my teachers, and... well, they usually said I was always out of my seat. And that I had a bad habit of talking before I was called on. I really wasn't trying to be disruptive, I promise! I think I just got really eager to participate, you know? They also wrote that I would rush through group activities, even when I totally understood the work and knew how to do it. I just wanted to get to the next thing, I guess. 

I was a good kid, really, just maybe a little too enthusiastic sometimes. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about?
Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day nearly every day?

Oh! Um, no, not at all. I mean, I get a little frustrated with myself when I can't keep my shop stuff straight, but I definitely don't feel hopeless. 

I'm actually a pretty upbeat person, I promise! I always try to look on the bright side. I really just get a bit stressed out because I want to do a good job with everything and not let anyone down. 

Is it... is it okay if I just feel a little overwhelmed sometimes, but not sad? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Before age 12, did you often have trouble paying attention in class or finishing schoolwork?

Um... no, I don't think so? I hope that's okay. I actually always made sure to finish my schoolwork. Like I mentioned a little bit ago, I would kind of speed through things sometimes because I just really wanted to move on to the next activity, but I always, always got it done! I really didn't want to upset my teachers or get a bad grade. 

And as for paying attention... I think I was pretty good at that? I mean, I was definitely a bit wiggly in my chair, but I always knew what the teacher was saying. I was listening really hard so I could participate. I wasn't really daydreaming or ignoring the lesson at all. 

Does... does that make sense? Like, is it helpful if I was paying attention, just maybe doing it a little too energetically?
In the past six months, have you found yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things most days?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think I worry excessively. I hope that's the right word for it. 

I definitely care about things, you know? Like, I want to make sure I'm doing a good job and that people are happy with me. But I wouldn't call it worrying all the time. It's more just... wanting to be responsible. I don't sit around stressing out about every little thing most days, I promise! I try to just stay positive and keep moving forward. 

Is it... is it normal to care a lot without it being like, a huge worry? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea about how I feel.
Did these problems with organization and paying attention continue into adulthood, or did they only start recently?

Um... well, it definitely hasn't been forever! Like I said, I was always really good at finishing my work when I was younger. 

I feel a little silly admitting this, but it really only became a... a real problem about two years and two months ago? That was when I changed schools, and I had to start managing my business program and my little accessories shop all at the same time. 

There just wasn't as much structure anymore, you know? Like, I didn't have teachers telling me exactly what to do and when, so keeping everything straight just got a little bit harder for me. But I'm trying really, really hard to get better at it, I promise! I always want to do a good job. 

Does that make sense? I hope it doesn't make me sound irresponsible... I just want to be totally honest with you about when it started getting tricky.
Before the age of 12, did you often make careless mistakes on schoolwork or other tasks?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. I mean, I always tried really, really hard to get everything right on my assignments. Even if I was going a little fast to get to the next thing, like I mentioned before, I... I didn't want to make silly mistakes because I didn't want my teachers or my parents to be disappointed in me. 

I cared a lot about getting good grades and being a good student, you know? So I always tried my absolute best to make sure my work was correct before I turned it in. I really didn't want anyone to think I was being sloppy. 

I hope that's okay? Like, I know you're asking about problems, but I really did try to be super careful back then. Is that the kind of information you need from me?
Do you often feel restless or find it hard to stay seated when you’re expected to be still?

Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm causing a disruption or anything, because I really do try my best to be polite and listen. 

But sometimes... yeah, even when I'm not actually going anywhere, I feel this sort of... buzzing in my body? It's like I just need to be moving, you know? Especially when I'm supposed to just sit still and listen, like in a class or a long meeting. It's not that I don't want to pay attention, I promise! It's just... my body feels a little bit like it has too much energy inside. 

I try to hide it, like maybe just wiggling my toes or shifting a little so I don't bother anyone. Is it bad that I feel that way? I hope it doesn't make me seem disrespectful when people are talking... I really am trying to be good about it!
Before age 12, were you often fidgety or unable to stay seated when you were supposed to be still?

Oh, um... gosh. I guess... well, yes. It's a little embarrassing to tell you this, but... my mom actually still has some of my old elementary school notes from my teachers. 

And, um, they used to write that I was always getting out of my seat. But I really wasn't trying to be naughty or cause trouble, I promise! I think I just got so excited and wanted to see what everyone else was doing, or I wanted to help out. 

The notes also said I had a habit of talking before I was called on, and kind of... rushing through our group activities. Which is silly, because they always said I completely understood the work! I just... I got so eager to share the answer or get to the next thing, you know? 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad student. I always wanted my teachers to be happy with me, and I felt awful if I ever interrupted them. Is... is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Do you often make careless mistakes because you miss details when doing schoolwork or tasks?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try really, really hard to pay attention to all the little details, especially if it's something important. 

I know you asked me about this when I was younger, too, and it's basically the same now. I always want to make sure I'm doing things exactly the way I'm supposed to, so I don't mess up and make people upset with me. Sometimes I might have to double-check things, but I really don't think I'm careless. I care a lot about doing a good job! 

I hope that's okay to say? I just... I don't want you to think I'm not trying my best, because I really am.
Do these attention and organization problems happen in more than one setting, such as both at school and at home or work?

Um... well, since I don't really have those kinds of attention problems, I guess it doesn't happen anywhere? 

I mean, I'm not working right now, and I just finished high school a little while ago, but when I was in school, I really tried to stay organized. And at home, I always try to keep my things neat so I don't bother my parents. I know sometimes my room gets a tiny bit messy if I'm in a hurry, but I always clean it up! I really try to be helpful around the house and not cause any stress. 

I hope I'm answering this right... I just don't want you to think I'm irresponsible or anything. I really do my best to keep track of my things and do what I'm supposed to do, wherever I am. Does that make sense?
Before age 12, did you often lose things you needed for school or other activities, like homework, books, or supplies?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I really tried to be careful with my things. 

My mom always helped me pack my backpack the night before, so I wouldn't forget anything important. And I always wanted to make sure I had my homework done and ready to turn in, because I loved getting gold stars and seeing my teachers smile. 

Sometimes, maybe... well, maybe a pencil would roll off my desk, or I'd misplace an eraser, but nothing big like a whole textbook or an important assignment. I always felt so terrible if I couldn't find something, so I really, really tried to keep track of it all. 

Is that what you mean? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples. I promise I was always trying to be a good student and take care of my things!
Do these organization or attention problems make it hard for you to function in daily life?

Um... well, since I don't really have those attention problems, it's not like they're ruining my life or anything. I mean, I really try my hardest to keep everything together! 

But... I guess... well, there was this one little mix-up recently. I'm trying to get into this program, and I kind of... I missed a few of the required steps. Just a silly mistake! But now they're saying my financial aid might be at risk, which is really stressful because I don't want to be a burden on anyone. And, um, sometimes when I'm helping out on shop projects with other people, I get a little too eager and maybe jump ahead or talk over them without meaning to... and I think they've started depending on me a little less because of it. 

I feel really awful about it, honestly. I'm trying so hard to fix it and show them I can be reliable. Do you think that means I'm doing something wrong? I promise I'm really trying to be good and do everything right!
Do you feel intense fear or anxiety when you’re around other people because you worry they’ll judge, embarrass, or criticize you?

Um... no, definitely not. I actually really like being around people! I always try my best to be friendly and outgoing so everyone feels comfortable. 

Like I mentioned before, sometimes I get a little *too* excited and maybe talk over people without meaning to—which I promise I am really, really trying to fix! But I don't feel scared of them or worry that they're going to be mean or criticize me. I just want to make sure everyone is having a good time and, well, I just want them to like me, you know? 

I hope that's okay... I just try to be a positive person to be around. Does that sound like a good thing?
When you’re in social situations, do you feel afraid that other people will judge you negatively?

Oh, um... I think that's kind of like what you just asked, right? But yeah, no, I really don't. 

I mean, I definitely want people to think good things about me—I think everyone wants that!—and I always try my absolute best to be a good friend and make people smile. But it's not like a scary feeling, or a deep fear that they're judging me, if that makes sense. I just genuinely love being around people and chatting with them. 

I hope I'm explaining it okay... Did I maybe say something wrong before to make you think I was scared of them? I promise I'm really comfortable in social situations!
When you have to speak up in class or in a group, do you ever feel afraid that you might say something embarrassing or that others will think badly of you?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I guess I'm pretty comfortable speaking up! Actually, sometimes I'm the first one to raise my hand or just blurt out an answer if I'm really excited about the topic. 

I know I probably shouldn't do that, and I'm really working on waiting my turn better, I promise! But it's not because I'm scared of being embarrassed or anything. I just... I like participating and helping keep the conversation going. 

I hope I'm giving you the right answers... I just don't really get that nervous about people thinking badly of me when I talk. Is that what you were looking for?
Do you avoid social situations because you’re afraid other people will judge you?

Oh, no, I definitely don't avoid them! I actually really look forward to hanging out with people. 

If anything, I'm usually the one trying to get everyone together to do something fun. I'd never want to stay home just because I was worried about what people thought of me. I really do try to get along with everyone and be someone they want to invite out. 

I mean, I hope that's coming across okay... I just really value my friends and being social. That's a good thing, right?
Before the past two years, did you ever have ongoing problems with disorganization or paying attention at home, school, or work?

Um, well... I wouldn't really say I had problems with paying attention or being disorganized, exactly. I mean, I've always been pretty good at understanding the work! 

But, um... I guess I've always had a lot of energy? Like, my mom actually still has these notes from my elementary school teachers... and they usually said things like I was out of my seat a lot, or that I'd talk before they called on me. And sometimes I'd rush through group activities, but that was just because I already got what we were supposed to be doing, you know? 

I really wasn't trying to be difficult or anything, I promise! I just got so eager to move on to the next thing. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid... I always tried my best to be good!
When you need to speak up in a group or class, do you ever hold back because you’re afraid of being embarrassed or judged?

Um, I think you might have asked me something similar just a minute ago? But no, I really don't hold back at all. 

I actually really like contributing to the class or group. I'm usually the one volunteering to read or, you know, getting the discussion going. I'm definitely not afraid of people judging me for talking. If anything, I probably talk a little too much sometimes, but I just get so enthusiastic! 

I really try to be a good participant, you know? I hope it's okay that my answer is the same as before... I just really don't get shy about that kind of thing.
When you're in a social situation, do you usually avoid speaking up because you're afraid people will notice mistakes or judge you?

Um, I think this is kind of like the other questions about being judged? So, um, no, I really don't avoid speaking up. 

I've never been the type to worry about making a mistake when I talk. I just kind of jump right in! I'm pretty comfortable around people, and I really just want to be friendly and keep the conversation going. I hope I'm answering this right... I just really don't have that fear of people noticing mistakes or anything. I just like being part of the group, you know? Is it okay that my answers are all kind of similar for these?
